reported.latency: p50, p95 and max, per request label

why_latency_is_not_enforced: There is no performance requirement in requirements/requirements-catalog.md
to enforce. Inventing a number here would put an SLA in the repository that
no requirement asked for and no stakeholder agreed, which is how a test
The figures are also dominated by where the database is rather than by the
application. A local run reaches Neon over the internet, so a single
transfer costs a few hundred milliseconds before the application does any
work, and twenty concurrent debits serialising on row locks over that link
measured p95 near 37 seconds. The same plan against the postgres:16
container CI starts in the runner is an order of magnitude faster. A
threshold that passes in one and fails in the other tests the network.
So latency is recorded every run and gated on nothing. To turn it into a
gate: collect a baseline from several CI runs, add PERF requirements to the
catalog with targets that baseline supports, then enforce those here. That
order matters — the requirement first, then the threshold.
what_is_enforced_and_why_it_travels: The correctness invariants hold on any machine at any speed. A concurrent
debit answering anything but 201 or 409, a 5xx, or a balance that does not
fall by exactly the amount plus fee of every success is a defect wherever
it appears. Those are safe to fail a build on.
